name: felix-heartbeat-gate-pre-rollout

subject.implementation: Pre-rollout: OpenClaw heartbeat invokes main agent (Sonnet 4.6) directly every ~30 minutes when HEARTBEAT.md has tasks; otherwise emits a silent ok-token without an LLM call.

methodology.summary: Walk the OpenClaw main-agent session JSONL(s) on office2, identify each heartbeat tick by the literal preamble OpenClaw injects ('Read HEARTBEAT.md if it exists (workspace context)...'), then sum the per-turn `usage` records WITHIN each tick. OpenClaw records the Anthropic-priced cost per turn in `usage.cost.total`; the baseline prefers that observed value over re-applying list-price math. Sonnet 4.6 list price is retained for fallback and for the post-rollout Haiku comparison. The measurement reflects only main-agent heartbeats — WhatsApp-triage turns and ESCALATE events from other paths are excluded by the preamble filter.
methodology.billing_model_note: We treat total_input_tokens_billable = input + cache_read + cache_write (cache-read and cache-write are charged at different per-token rates but all consume the input-side quota). When OpenClaw's `usage.cost.total` field is present on the assistant turn, that priced value is summed directly and `cost_source = observed-from-session-log`.
reproduction_steps: 4. Spot-check the tick_count against the OpenClaw heartbeat cadence and HEARTBEAT.md fill rate (only ticks with non-template HEARTBEAT.md content produce an LLM call; the empty-skip rule short-circuits most ticks to silent ok-token).
5. Promote into the baselines directory: `cp /tmp/baseline.json docs/design/architecture/baselines/felix-heartbeat-gate-pre-rollout.json` and commit.
methodology.sample_size_guidance: Target ≥7 days of natural traffic to absorb day-of-week variation in HEARTBEAT.md fill state. The captured 14-day window deliberately ends at 2026-05-19, two days before the Anthropic API spend cap began returning 400 errors on 2026-05-22 — including post-cap days would dilute the per-tick cost with zero-token error turns and bias the daily-rate denominator. For re-measurement after 2026-06-01 (cap reset), bound `--window-end` at a pre-cap or post-reset boundary.

open_caveats: Heartbeat cadence is ~30 min (48 ticks/day at full rate), but the observed rate is 5.07 ticks/day across the 14-day window. This is because the current heartbeat short-circuits to a silent `ok-token` when HEARTBEAT.md is empty/template-only (the existing 'empty = skip' rule per spec.md line 64), so only ticks where Kent placed a scheduled task in `/data/services/openclaw/data/HEARTBEAT.md` produce an LLM call and show up in the session JSONL. The 5/day figure therefore represents the operational LLM-touching rate, not the underlying tick cadence. Post-rollout NFR-001 comparison must use the SAME definition (gate-touching ticks) to be apples-to-apples.

OpenClaw's `usage.cost.total` field is the observed-priced cost at session-write time. It matches Anthropic's pricing for Sonnet 4.6 and aligns within 2.6% of the re-derived list-price math (observed $1.69 vs list-price $1.65 on the same tokens), so the observed value is the authoritative cost source. The small delta is from Anthropic's cache-write pricing currently differing slightly from list-price input rate.

The post-rollout WP-04 measurement reads `gate-ledger.jsonl` (Haiku gate decisions) plus any escalation cost from the OpenClaw session log. The acceptance threshold is `post-rollout daily cost / pre-rollout daily cost ≤ 0.20`. Pre-rollout daily cost = $1.69 / 14d ≈ $0.121/day → post-rollout daily cost must be ≤ $0.024/day to satisfy NFR-001.

Excluded from this measurement: WhatsApp-triage turns on the main agent (NO_REPLY / HEARTBEAT_OK responses to inbound messages), ESCALATE-event turns from `openclaw system event`, and any LLM traffic not routed through OpenClaw. The preamble filter ('Read HEARTBEAT.md if it exists') matches only the cron-driven heartbeat injection.

100 session JSONL files were walked (including `.reset.*` and `.deleted.*` rotation artifacts); OpenClaw rolls the active session at 04:00 UTC daily, so a single day's heartbeats may straddle multiple files. The aggregation handles this transparently.
